asker_query: Madam, Lakshmi-ji has very bad pain in her back since 30 minutes. She is crying. What should I give her?
answer:
It is distressing to see Lakshmi-ji in such severe pain.
For a patient already on scheduled Morphine SR (Sustained Release), a sudden breakthrough of 8/10 pain requires immediate attention.
You should contact her palliative care physician or the nearest pain clinic immediately to request a "rescue dose" of immediate-release (IR) morphine.
According to the WHO Pain Relief Ladder and NPPC guidelines, pain must be managed "by the clock" and titrated to the individual; there is no standard upper limit for cancer pain, and doses can be increased as the disease advances.
In your home setting, your primary goal is to ensure comfort while waiting for medical guidance.
While you await the physician's instructions for a rescue dose, you can assist Lakshmi-ji by using non-pharmacological methods to help manage her distress, such as careful repositioning, providing reassurance, or using cold/warm packs if she finds them soothing.
Ensure she continues her prescribed laxative (Lactulose), as constipation is a common side effect of morphine that can worsen abdominal and back discomfort.
If you notice new red flags—such as sudden weakness in her legs, numbness in the groin area, or loss of bowel/bladder control—this is a medical emergency (potential spinal cord compression) and she must be taken to the nearest hospital immediately.
When administering morphine, always remember that it is a safe and effective gold standard for severe cancer pain when used under supervision.
To prevent side effects, ensure she is also taking an anti-emetic if she experiences nausea.
Remember that increasing doses for escalating cancer pain is a standard part of palliative care and does not mean she is becoming addicted.
Always keep a record of the pain intensity and the timing of all medications to share with her doctor during the next review.

_(The specific amount and schedule of any medicine are not included here. Take that part of your question to your next consultation.)_
